# Substance Extraction - Evaluation (Stage C)

*Generated by `src/evaluate_extraction.py`.*

## Label provenance (read this first)

**All reference labels in this report were produced by an AI assistant (Claude), not by a human annotator.** The AI read each sampled text and wrote the substances it names, following the guideline below, without looking at the regex output. Because the same AI system also wrote the extraction rules, the two are **not fully independent**, and the metrics below are an *agreement check*, not a validated accuracy figure. The project owner can confirm or correct each label in `data/review/substance_review_for_owner.xlsx`; re-running the script will then use the human labels.

## Design

- Unit of evaluation: distinct risk text (60 sampled at random, seed 42, from the distinct texts in the dataset), covering 152 alerts.
- Guideline: label every specific chemical substance or named microorganism the text says the product contains; do not label class words (corticosteroid, nitrosamine, allergenic fragrances).
- Metrics: precision = share of extracted items that are correct; recall = share of labelled items that were found; F1 = harmonic mean; exact match = share of texts where the extracted set equals the labelled set.

## Pretrained model comparison

- Model: [OpenMed/OpenMed-NER-ChemicalDetect-PubMed-109M](https://huggingface.co/OpenMed/OpenMed-NER-ChemicalDetect-PubMed-109M), revision `78f35d736474`, licence Apache-2.0 (from the model card).
- Training domain (model card): BC4CHEMD - chemical mentions in PubMed abstracts. Safety Gate texts are short regulatory sentences with consumer-facing wording, abbreviations in brackets and occasional typos, so domain transfer is not guaranteed.
- Run locally on CPU; no data leaves the machine. Model weights are not redistributed in this repository.
- On all 155 distinct texts, the model and the rules produce the same chemical set for 129 texts (1684 of 1714 alerts). Disagreements: `data/evaluation/rule_vs_model_disagreements.csv`.
- Items found **only by the model** (all texts): `2-(4-tert-buylbenzyl) propionaldehe`, `azodyes`, `corticosteroid`, `nitrosamine`, `phthalate`, `prostaglandin`. On manual inspection these are class words (e.g. corticosteroid, phthalate, prostaglandin) or a misspelt name already covered by its abbreviation - no new substance was discovered.
- Items found **only by the rules**: `Lead` (6 texts), `Centella asiatica extract` (1 texts). The model does not tag the metal *lead*; the hedged plant extract is a rule-based 'uncertain' item.

**Why the rule-based score is 1.0.** The dictionary was written for this export, and the AI reference labels come from the same AI system that wrote the rules. A perfect score here shows internal consistency, not real-world accuracy.

**Interpretation.** The rule-based dictionary is tuned to this export and therefore scores higher on it; that is expected and is also its weakness (it only knows substances someone has added). The model needs no dictionary and can surface new substance names, but it misses some short or ambiguous names. A practical design is: dictionary for reporting, model as a *discovery* step whose new findings go into the review queue.

## Limitations

- Small sample (60 distinct texts); BMHCA sentences dominate the alert-weighted figures.
- Reference labels are AI-produced until reviewed by the owner.
- Exact-name matching: a correct mention with a different canonical name would count as an error.
- The dictionary was developed on the same export that is evaluated here (no held-out data). New exports are the real test.
